key_insight: Perovskite-based tandem photovoltaics could enable higher-efficiency solar power while improving circularity through simpler architectures, lower-temperature processing, and easier material recovery than conventional c-Si systems.
engineering_relevance: The paper informs how to design tandem PV manufacturing, recycling, and policy frameworks that scale to terawatt deployment without creating an unsustainable waste burden.
method: Reviewed circularity challenges across the full PV lifecycle
Analyzed materials, technoeconomic, and policy dimensions beyond standard lifecycle assessments
Outlined strategies for substitution of scarce materials, recycling, delamination, and lead sequestration
evidence_signal: The abstract cites projected c-Si waste of about 160 million tonnes by 2050 and uses that scale to motivate circular design requirements for perovskite tandems.
watch_item: Real-world deployment still depends on proving scalable, cost-effective recycling and safe lead management at commercial module volumes.
paper_title: Circularity in Perovskite-Based Tandem Photovoltaics for Terawatt-Scale Deployment
